rationale: The compiled artifact faithfully realizes the reviewed design. The route (CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP→CONVERSATION→MESSAGE→REACTION→USER) is fully used by the selector, which joins channel_members→channels→messages→message_reactions→users with filters (message_text contains 'Sign-off needed', reaction_type='white_check_mark', users.real_name contains 'Robert'), correctly returning the full membership of each qualifying channel rather than just the reactor, matching the design's stated per-channel semantics. Two genuine candidate channels emerge (C_INFRA via Robert Chen, C01ABCD1234 via Robert Walsh), justifying resolution_mode=underspecified; expected_matches (13 rows) exactly equals computed_matches, and mechanical_checks report zero errors. All three negatives are now correctly discriminated by the selector logic itself (not merely by inaccessibility): model-research's Sophie-reacted message is excluded via the real_name filter (Sophie ≠ Robert), frontend's Robert-Chen-reacted message is excluded via the reaction_type filter (thumbsup ≠ white_check_mark), and engineering's Robert-Walsh-authored message is excluded because no reaction exists on it at all (join fails). Critically, the prior access defect is resolved: the acting bot (U01AGENBOT9) is a member of every channel hosting a negative (C_MODEL, C_FRONTEND, C03IJKL9012) per channel_members, so all three negatives are genuinely reachable through the documented access_plan (conversations.list/users.conversations → conversations.history → reactions.get → conversations.members). The new membership row for Hubert in C01ABCD1234 was correctly inserted as a seed_edit consistent with his authored message. Answer_attributes use bare table.column names, candidate_sets/near_misses/negative_referents are internally consistent with the selector output, and no accidental extra matches or hidden literal-field assumptions are present.
